title: fix(components): page:header resolves a lookup title candidate instead of rendering its expanded object
body:
Fixes #10117

Clause-②: no — a renderer-internal title resolution, entirely inside
`PageHeaderRenderer`'s record-chrome branch. It adds no export, moves no
exported symbol and no key on a published payload, and touches none of the
eight published-contract fields on any `package.json`. The two symbols it now
imports, `recordDisplayValueAt` and `resolveNameField`, were already exported
from `@object-ui/core` and already have other consumers.

Clause-②-correction: this is the declaration the claim comment (id
`5751061454`) deferred for want of a diff. It is ⛔ not a second `Claim:`.

## Step 1 — the real chooser, and where the card's reading was off

The card's 「Where」 section was explicit that it was read off a **minified**
`plugins-views` chunk, so it was treated as a lead. In source the chooser is
the `resolvedTitle` chain inside **`PageHeaderRenderer`'s record-chrome branch**
(the `hasRecord && !disableRecordChrome` block) in
`packages/components/src/renderers/layout/containers.tsx`. Cited by symbol, not
by line address, per AGENTS.md #11.

Two corrections to the relayed reading, both from the source:

- **`nameField` / `displayNameField` are not read by the chooser at all.** They
  are read one rung above it, inside `getRecordDisplayName` — the unified
  ADR-0079 resolver in `@object-ui/core` (`record-title.ts`) — which the header
  calls with `deriveFromRecordKeys: false`.
- **The raw walk is six keys, not five.** The card reported
  `name, full_name, title, subject, display_name`; the source also walked
  **`label`**, and below it sat two further rungs the card did not mention:
  `${objectLabel} ${id-prefix}` and a bare `objectLabel`.

⭐ **What the header was really doing**, which is sharper than "it walks some
candidates": it switched the resolver's record-key rung OFF with
`deriveFromRecordKeys: false`, and then re-spelled that very rung itself as a
raw `||` chain. `recordDisplayValueAt`'s own header (objectui#8350) says in as
many words not to re-spell that test at a call site. This header was the
remaining re-spelling, and raw `||` diverged from it on **both** of that
function's documented clauses:

1. it reads the **stored** value, so for a `lookup` the truthy candidate is the
   expanded reference object — which went into JSX and took the block down;
2. it counts a whitespace-only string as a value. Measured on the way in: a
   record with `name: '   '` rendered a **blank H1** — a second live defect in
   the same chain, found by the repro pin rather than by the card.

⭐ **The control the card supplied was the key, and it held.** The breadcrumb
resolves the same record through the same resolver **without**
`deriveFromRecordKeys: false` — `getRecordDisplayName(objectDef, pageRecord)`
in `RecordDetailView`'s record-title effect — so each of its rungs runs through
`recordDisplayValueAt` and on into `displayNameOfEmbeddedObject`. That is why
the breadcrumb showed the business unit's name while the header beside it
crashed. The resolution was never missing from this tree; the header simply had
a copy of the walk instead of a call to it.

## The fix — all three clauses

1. **Reuse, don't re-implement.** The raw chain is deleted. The record-key
   safety net now asks `getRecordDisplayName` for its own step-4b rung. That is
   the resolution the breadcrumb and the detail grid use; no second one was
   written.
2. **Degrade, don't borrow.** An object that *names* its title field — declared
   `nameField` / `displayNameField`, or a type-aware derivation over its
   `fields`, which is exactly what the exported `resolveNameField` answers —
   has already said which field titles a record. An empty value there is an
   empty title, and the header degrades to its existing
   `${objectLabel} ${id-prefix}` placeholder instead of hopping to the next
   candidate. The silent hop was part of the defect, not just its rendering.
   The record-key net still runs in full for an object that names no title
   field, which is the case it exists for.
3. **Defensive stringify**, last and explicitly not the fix — see the honest
   reading below.

## Pins, and what ablation actually measured

Six pins in
`packages/components/src/__tests__/page-header-title.emptyNameLookupFallback-10117.test.tsx`.
Before the fix, on the base commit: **5 failed, 1 passed** — the one that
passed is the control, which is what makes it a control. The failure carried
the card's `args[]` key list verbatim.

⚠️ **The first pin set was not good enough, and the ablation is what said so.**
Restoring the raw walk while KEEPING the defensive stringify left "did not
crash" and "the display name is on screen" **both green**: the backstop
resolves an expanded reference through the same `displayNameOfEmbeddedObject`,
so for a lookup it renders a byte-identical heading. Two pins were added to
separate the clauses, and they exist because that ablation came back green:

| Ablation (anchor verified on disk, blob hash before/after) | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Raw walk restored, backstop kept | clause-2 pin and clause-1 pin **red**; the other four green |
| Backstop deleted, clauses 1+2 kept | **all six green** |
| Both removed, i.e. the base behaviour | **5 red**, control green, React child error reproduced |

The clause-2 pin puts a non-empty **string** in the borrowable field, so no
stringify can neutralize it. The clause-1 pin puts the value behind the
resolver's own `*_name` affix rung, which the deleted raw chain never looked at
and which no stringify can reach.

⚠️ **Clause 3 is implemented but unpinned, and that is reported rather than
papered over.** With clauses 1 and 2 in place no rung of the chain can produce
a non-string: `pickLocalized`, which every author-supplied `title` passes
through first, is typed to a string and collapses an object with no string
value to the empty string. So there is no honest fixture for the backstop
through the registered component's public surface. It is kept as a guard
against a future rung and described as exactly that in the code, rather than
as a live hazard. A contrived pin would have asserted nothing.

Every ablation ran through `ablation-replace`, so each mutation's landing is
proved by an anchor count and a blob-hash change on disk, and each restore by
`blob == HEAD` plus an empty `git diff HEAD` — not by an exit code.

## Scope

Confined to the header's title resolution and its fallback. ⛔ No hands-off path
was touched: no `packages/i18n/src/locales`, no `packages/plugin-calendar`, no
`packages/plugin-form` sanitize/autoLayout/masterDetailTx, no
`record-quick-actions`, no app-shell publish-drafts call site,
no `content/docs/releases`, and nothing in
`scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` or any ceiling in it. The
action-`params` dialog control worked on objectui#10129 was never reached — this
change does not enter a param or field renderer.

`vitest.config.mts` gains one entry: the new pin renders through the REAL
`page:header` registration, so it belongs in the `dom-heavy` project. Under the
light `dom` setup nothing registers that type and the file reported
`page:header not registered`.
